description: Adversaries may execute malicious payloads via loading shared modules. Shared modules are executable files that are loaded into processes to provide access to reusable code, such as specific custom functions or invoking OS API functions (i.e., Native API).

name: Data Encoding
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Data Encoding in C2 Channels
description: Adversaries may encode data to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect. Command and control (C2) information can be encoded using a standard data encoding system.

name: Standard Encoding
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1132.001 Data Encoding: Standard Encoding (Base64/Hex/MIME) across Windows, Linux, macOS, ESXi
description: Adversaries may encode data with a standard data encoding system to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect. Command and control (C2) information can be encoded using a standard data encoding system that adheres to existing protocol specifications.

name: Non-Standard Encoding
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1132.002 Data Encoding: Non-Standard Encoding across Windows, Linux, macOS, ESXi
description: Adversaries may encode data with a non-standard data encoding system to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect. Command and control (C2) information can be encoded using a non-standard data encoding system that diverges from existing protocol specifications.

name: External Remote Services

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1133 External Remote Services across Windows, Linux, macOS, Containers
description: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access and/or persist within a network. Remote services such as VPNs, Citrix, and other access mechanisms allow users to connect to internal enterprise network resources from external locations.

name: Access Token Manipulation
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1134 Access Token Manipulation on Windows
description: Adversaries may modify access tokens to operate under a different user or system security context to perform actions and bypass access controls. Windows uses access tokens to determine the ownership of a running process.

name: Token Impersonation/Theft
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1134.001 Access Token Manipulation: Token Impersonation/Theft on Windows
description: Adversaries may duplicate then impersonate another user's existing token to escalate privileges and bypass access controls. For example, an adversary can duplicate an existing token using `DuplicateToken` or `DuplicateTokenEx`.

name: Create Process with Token
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1134.002 Create Process with Token (Windows)
description: Adversaries may create a new process with an existing token to escalate privileges and bypass access controls. Processes can be created with the token and resulting security context of another user using features such as CreateProcessWithTokenW and runas.

name: Make and Impersonate Token
detection_strategies: Behavior‑chain detection for T1134.003 Make and Impersonate Token (Windows)
description: Adversaries may make new tokens and impersonate users to escalate privileges and bypass access controls. For example, if an adversary has a username and password but the user is not logged onto the system the adversary can then create a logon session for the user using the `LogonUser` function.

name: Parent PID Spoofing
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1134.004 Access Token Manipulation: Parent PID Spoofing (Windows)
description: Adversaries may spoof the parent process identifier (PPID) of a new process to evade process-monitoring defenses or to elevate privileges. New processes are typically spawned directly from their parent, or calling, process unless explicitly specified.

name: SID-History Injection
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1134.005 Access Token Manipulation: SID-History Injection (Windows)
description: Adversaries may use SID-History Injection to escalate privileges and bypass access controls. The Windows security identifier (SID) is a unique value that identifies a user or group account. SIDs are used by Windows security in both security descriptors and access tokens.

name: Network Share Discovery
detection_strategies: Behavior-chain detection for T1135 Network Share Discovery across Windows, Linux, and macOS
description: Adversaries may look for folders and drives shared on remote systems as a means of identifying sources of information to gather as a precursor for Collection and to identify potential systems of interest for Lateral Movement.

name: Create Account
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1136 - Create Account across platforms
description: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to victim systems. With a sufficient level of access, creating such accounts may be used to establish secondary credentialed access that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

name: Local Account
detection_strategies: T1136.001 Detection Strategy - Local Account Creation Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access to victim systems. Local accounts are those configured by an organization for use by users, remote support, services, or for administration on a single system or service.

name: Domain Account
detection_strategies: T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may create a domain account to maintain access to victim systems. Domain accounts are those managed by Active Directory Domain Services where access and permissions are configured across systems and services that are part of that domain. Domain accounts can cover user, administrator, and service accounts.

name: Cloud Account
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1136.003 - Cloud Account Creation across IaaS, IdP, SaaS, Office
description: Adversaries may create a cloud account to maintain access to victim systems. With a sufficient level of access, such accounts may be used to establish secondary credentialed access that does not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

name: Office Application Startup

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detect Office Startup-Based Persistence via Macros, Forms, and Registry Hooks
description: Adversaries may leverage Microsoft Office-based applications for persistence between startups. Microsoft Office is a fairly common application suite on Windows-based operating systems within an enterprise network.

name: Office Template Macros

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detect Persistence via Office Template Macro Injection or Registry Hijack
description: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Office templates to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Microsoft Office contains templates that are part of common Office applications and are used to customize styles. The base templates within the application are used each time an application starts.

name: Office Test
detection_strategies: Detect Persistence via Office Test Registry DLL Injection
description: Adversaries may abuse the Microsoft Office "Office Test" Registry key to obtain persistence on a compromised system. An Office Test Registry location exists that allows a user to specify an arbitrary DLL that will be executed every time an Office application is started.

name: Outlook Forms
detection_strategies: Detect Persistence via Outlook Custom Forms Triggered by Malicious Email
description: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook forms to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook forms are used as templates for presentation and functionality in Outlook messages.

name: Outlook Home Page
detection_strategies: Detect Persistence via Outlook Home Page Exploitation
description: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook's Home Page feature to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook Home Page is a legacy feature used to customize the presentation of Outlook folders. This feature allows for an internal or external URL to be loaded and presented whenever a folder is opened.

name: Outlook Rules
detection_strategies: Detect Persistence via Malicious Outlook Rules
description: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook rules to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook rules allow a user to define automated behavior to manage email messages.

name: Add-ins
detection_strategies: Detect Persistence via Malicious Office Add-ins
description: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Office add-ins to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Office add-ins can be used to add functionality to Office programs.

name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
detection_strategies: Detect Adversary Deobfuscation or Decoding of Files and Payloads
description: Adversaries may use Obfuscated Files or Information to hide artifacts of an intrusion from analysis. They may require separate mechanisms to decode or deobfuscate that information depending on how they intend to use it.

name: Software Extensions
detection_strategies: Detection of Malicious or Unauthorized Software Extensions
description: Adversaries may abuse software extensions to establish persistent access to victim systems. Software extensions are modular components that enhance or customize the functionality of software applications, including web browsers, Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), and other platforms.

name: Browser Extensions
detection_strategies: Detecting Malicious Browser Extensions Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may abuse internet browser extensions to establish persistent access to victim systems. Browser extensions or plugins are small programs that can add functionality to and customize aspects of internet browsers.

name: IDE Extensions
detection_strategies: Detect malicious IDE extension install/usage and IDE tunneling
description: Adversaries may abuse an integrated development environment (IDE) extension to establish persistent access to victim systems.

name: Browser Session Hijacking
detection_strategies: Detect browser session hijacking via privilege, handle access, and remote thread into browsers
description: Adversaries may take advantage of security vulnerabilities and inherent functionality in browser software to change content, modify user-behaviors, and intercept information as part of various browser session hijacking techniques.

name: Forced Authentication
detection_strategies: Detect Forced SMB/WebDAV Authentication via lure files and outbound NTLM
description: Adversaries may gather credential material by invoking or forcing a user to automatically provide authentication information through a mechanism in which they can intercept.

name: Drive-by Compromise
detection_strategies: Drive-by Compromise — Behavior-based, Multi-platform Detection Strategy (T1189)
description: Adversaries may gain access to a system through a user visiting a website over the normal course of browsing.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Exploit Public-Facing Application – multi-signal correlation (request → error → post-exploit process/egress)
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network. The weakness in the system can be a software bug, a temporary glitch, or a misconfiguration.

name: Supply Chain Compromise
detection_strategies: Behavioral detection for Supply Chain Compromise (package/update tamper → install → first-run)
description: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
detection_strategies: Supply-chain tamper in dependencies/dev-tools (manager→write/install→first-run→egress)
description: Adversaries may manipulate software dependencies and development tools prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise. Applications often depend on external software to function properly.

name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
detection_strategies: Compromised software/update chain (installer/write → first-run/child → egress/signature anomaly)
description: Adversaries may manipulate application software prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

name: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
detection_strategies: Hardware Supply Chain Compromise Detection via Host Status & Boot Integrity Checks
description: Adversaries may manipulate hardware components in products prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

name: BITS Jobs
detection_strategies: Detect abuse of Windows BITS Jobs for download, execution and persistence
description: Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs to persistently execute code and perform various background tasks. Windows Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) is a low-bandwidth, asynchronous file transfer mechanism exposed through Component Object Model (COM).

name: Trusted Relationship
detection_strategies: Detect abuse of Trusted Relationships (third-party and delegated admin access)
description: Adversaries may breach or otherwise leverage organizations who have access to intended victims. Access through trusted third party relationship abuses an existing connection that may not be protected or receives less scrutiny than standard mechanisms of gaining access to a network.

name: Hardware Additions

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Detect unauthorized or suspicious Hardware Additions (USB/Thunderbolt/Network)
description: Adversaries may physically introduce computer accessories, networking hardware, or other computing devices into a system or network that can be used as a vector to gain access. Rather than just connecting and distributing payloads via removable storage (i.e.

name: Password Policy Discovery
detection_strategies: Password Policy Discovery – cross-platform behavior-chain analytics
description: Adversaries may attempt to access detailed information about the password policy used within an enterprise network or cloud environment. Password policies are a way to enforce complex passwords that are difficult to guess or crack through Brute Force.

name: Indirect Command Execution
detection_strategies: Indirect Command Execution – Windows utility abuse behavior chain
description: Adversaries may abuse utilities that allow for command execution to bypass security restrictions that limit the use of command-line interpreters. Various Windows utilities may be used to execute commands, possibly without invoking cmd.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
detection_strategies: Exploitation for Client Execution – cross-platform behavior chain (browser/Office/3rd-party apps)
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code. Vulnerabilities can exist in software due to unsecure coding practices that can lead to unanticipated behavior.

name: User Execution
detection_strategies: User Execution – multi-surface behavior chain (documents/links → helper/unpacker → LOLBIN/child → egress)
description: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to execute malicious code by, for example, opening a malicious document file or link. These user actions will typically be observed as follow-on behavior from forms of Phishing.

name: Malicious Link
detection_strategies: User Execution – Malicious Link (click → suspicious egress → download/write → follow-on activity)
description: An adversary may rely upon a user clicking a malicious link in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to click on a link that will lead to code execution. This user action will typically be observed as follow-on behavior from Spearphishing Link.

name: Malicious File
detection_strategies: User Execution – Malicious File via download/open → spawn chain (T1204.002)
description: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to open a file that will lead to code execution. This user action will typically be observed as follow-on behavior from Spearphishing Attachment.

name: Malicious Image
detection_strategies: User Execution – Malicious Image (containers & IaaS) – pull/run → start → anomalous behavior (T1204.003)
description: Adversaries may rely on a user running a malicious image to facilitate execution. Amazon Web Services (AWS) Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Images, and Azure Images as well as popular container runtimes such as Docker can be backdoored.

name: Malicious Copy and Paste
detection_strategies: User Execution – Malicious Copy & Paste (browser/email → shell with obfuscated one-liner) – T1204.004
description: An adversary may rely upon a user copying and pasting code in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to copy and paste code directly into a Command and Scripting Interpreter.

name: Malicious Library
detection_strategies: User-Initiated Malicious Library Installation via Package Manager (T1204.005)
description: Adversaries may rely on a user installing a malicious library to facilitate execution. Threat actors may Upload Malware to package managers such as NPM and PyPi, as well as to public code repositories such as GitHub.

name: Traffic Signaling

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Traffic Signaling (Port-knock / magic-packet → firewall or service activation) – T1205
description: Adversaries may use traffic signaling to hide open ports or other malicious functionality used for persistence or command and control.

name: Port Knocking
detection_strategies: Port-knock → rule/daemon change → first successful connect (T1205.001)
description: Adversaries may use port knocking to hide open ports used for persistence or command and control. To enable a port, an adversary sends a series of attempted connections to a predefined sequence of closed ports.

name: Socket Filters
detection_strategies: Socket-filter trigger → on-host raw-socket activity → reverse connection (T1205.002)
description: Adversaries may attach filters to a network socket to monitor then activate backdoors used for persistence or command and control.

name: Rogue Domain Controller
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Rogue Domain Controller (DCShadow) Registration and Replication Abuse
description: Adversaries may register a rogue Domain Controller to enable manipulation of Active Directory data. DCShadow may be used to create a rogue Domain Controller (DC).

name: Exploitation of Remote Services

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Exploitation of Remote Services – multi-platform lateral movement detection
description: Adversaries may exploit remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems once inside of a network.

name: Exploitation for Defense Evasion
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Exploitation for Defense Evasion
description: Adversaries may exploit a system or application vulnerability to bypass security features. Exploitation of a vulnerability occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to execute adversary-controlled code.

name: Exploitation for Credential Access
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Exploitation for Credential Access
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to collect credentials. Exploitation of a software vulnerability occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to execute adversary-controlled code.

name: Data from Information Repositories
detection_strategies: Abuse of Information Repositories for Data Collection
description: Adversaries may leverage information repositories to mine valuable information.

name: Confluence
detection_strategies: Programmatic and Excessive Access to Confluence Documentation
description: Adversaries may leverage Confluence repositories to mine valuable information.

name: Sharepoint
detection_strategies: Detecting Abnormal SharePoint Data Mining by Privileged or Rare Users
description: Adversaries may leverage the SharePoint repository as a source to mine valuable information. SharePoint will often contain useful information for an adversary to learn about the structure and functionality of the internal network and systems.

name: Code Repositories
detection_strategies: Detecting Bulk or Anomalous Access to Private Code Repositories via SaaS Platforms
description: Adversaries may leverage code repositories to collect valuable information. Code repositories are tools/services that store source code and automate software builds. They may be hosted internally or privately on third party sites such as Github, GitLab, SourceForge, and BitBucket.

name: Customer Relationship Management Software
detection_strategies: Detecting Suspicious Access to CRM Data in SaaS Environments
description: Adversaries may leverage Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software to mine valuable information. CRM software is used to assist organizations in tracking and managing customer interactions, as well as storing customer data.

name: Messaging Applications
detection_strategies: Detecting Unauthorized Collection from Messaging Applications in SaaS and Office Environments
description: Adversaries may leverage chat and messaging applications, such as Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, and Slack, to mine valuable information.

name: Databases
detection_strategies: Suspicious Database Access and Dump Activity Across Environments (T1213.006)
description: Adversaries may leverage databases to mine valuable information. These databases may be hosted on-premises or in the cloud (both in platform-as-a-service and software-as-a-service environments).

name: System Script Proxy Execution
detection_strategies: Detection of Script-Based Proxy Execution via Signed Microsoft Utilities
description: Adversaries may use trusted scripts, often signed with certificates, to proxy the execution of malicious files. Several Microsoft signed scripts that have been downloaded from Microsoft or are default on Windows installations can be used to proxy execution of other files.

name: PubPrn
detection_strategies: Detecting Remote Script Proxy Execution via PubPrn.vbs
description: Adversaries may use PubPrn to proxy execution of malicious remote files. PubPrn.vbs is a Visual Basic script that publishes a printer to Active Directory Domain Services. The script may be signed by Microsoft and is commonly executed through the Windows Command Shell via Cscript.exe.

name: SyncAppvPublishingServer
detection_strategies: Detecting PowerShell Execution via SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs Proxy Abuse
description: Adversaries may abuse SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to proxy execution of malicious PowerShell commands. SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs is a Visual Basic script associated with how Windows virtualizes applications (Microsoft Application Virtualization, or App-V).

name: Browser Information Discovery
detection_strategies: Detection of Local Browser Artifact Access for Reconnaissance
description: Adversaries may enumerate information about browsers to learn more about compromised environments.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection of Proxy Execution via Trusted Signed Binaries Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may bypass process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious content with signed, or otherwise trusted, binaries.

name: Compiled HTML File
detection_strategies: Detection of Suspicious Compiled HTML File Execution via hh.exe
description: Adversaries may abuse Compiled HTML files (.chm) to conceal malicious code. CHM files are commonly distributed as part of the Microsoft HTML Help system.

name: Control Panel
detection_strategies: Detection of Malicious Control Panel Item Execution via control.exe or Rundll32
description: Adversaries may abuse control.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. The Windows Control Panel process binary (control.exe) handles execution of Control Panel items, which are utilities that allow users to view and adjust computer settings.

name: CMSTP

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection of Malicious Profile Installation via CMSTP.exe
description: Adversaries may abuse CMSTP to proxy execution of malicious code. The Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (CMSTP.exe) is a command-line program used to install Connection Manager service profiles.

name: InstallUtil

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection of Malicious Code Execution via InstallUtil.exe
description: Adversaries may use InstallUtil to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. InstallUtil is a command-line utility that allows for installation and uninstallation of resources by executing specific installer components specified in .NET binaries.

name: Mshta

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detecting Mshta-based Proxy Execution via Suspicious HTA or Script Invocation
description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious .hta files and Javascript or VBScript through a trusted Windows utility.

name: Msiexec

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection of Msiexec Abuse for Local, Network, and DLL Execution
description: Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. Msiexec.exe is the command-line utility for the Windows Installer and is thus commonly associated with executing installation packages (.msi). The Msiexec.exe binary may also be digitally signed by Microsoft.

name: Odbcconf

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detecting Odbcconf Proxy Execution of Malicious DLLs
description: Adversaries may abuse odbcconf.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. Odbcconf.exe is a Windows utility that allows you to configure Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) drivers and data source names. The Odbcconf.exe binary may be digitally signed by Microsoft.

name: Regsvcs/Regasm

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detecting .NET COM Registration Abuse via Regsvcs/Regasm
description: Adversaries may abuse Regsvcs and Regasm to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. Regsvcs and Regasm are Windows command-line utilities that are used to register .NET Component Object Model (COM) assemblies. Both are binaries that may be digitally signed by Microsoft.

name: Regsvr32
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
description: Adversaries may abuse Regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code. Regsvr32.exe is a command-line program used to register and unregister object linking and embedding controls, including dynamic link libraries (DLLs), on Windows systems. The Regsvr32.exe binary may also be signed by Microsoft.

name: Rundll32
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1218.011 Rundll32 Abuse
description: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code. Using rundll32.exe, vice executing directly (i.e. Shared Modules), may avoid triggering security tools that may not monitor execution of the rundll32.exe process because of allowlists or false positives from normal operations.

name: Verclsid

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1218.012 Verclsid Abuse
description: Adversaries may abuse verclsid.exe to proxy execution of malicious code. Verclsid.exe is known as the Extension CLSID Verification Host and is responsible for verifying each shell extension before they are used by Windows Explorer or the Windows Shell. Adversaries may abuse verclsid.exe to execute malicious payloads.

name: Mavinject

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detecting Code Injection via mavinject.exe (App-V Injector)
description: Adversaries may abuse mavinject.exe to proxy execution of malicious code. Mavinject.exe is the Microsoft Application Virtualization Injector, a Windows utility that can inject code into external processes as part of Microsoft Application Virtualization (App-V).

name: MMC

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detecting MMC (.msc) Proxy Execution and Malicious COM Activation
description: Adversaries may abuse mmc.exe to proxy execution of malicious .msc files. Microsoft Management Console (MMC) is a binary that may be signed by Microsoft and is used in several ways in either its GUI or in a command prompt.

name: Electron Applications

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detecting Electron Application Abuse for Proxy Execution
description: Adversaries may abuse components of the Electron framework to execute malicious code. The Electron framework hosts many common applications such as Signal, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

name: Remote Access Tools

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Behavior-Chain Detection for Remote Access Tools (Tool-Agnostic)
description: An adversary may use legitimate remote access tools to establish an interactive command and control channel within a network.

name: IDE Tunneling
detection_strategies: IDE Tunneling Detection via Process, File, and Network Behaviors
description: Adversaries may abuse Integrated Development Environment (IDE) software with remote development features to establish an interactive command and control channel on target systems within a network.

name: Remote Desktop Software

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Remote Desktop Software Execution and Beaconing Detection
description: An adversary may use legitimate desktop support software to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.

name: Remote Access Hardware
detection_strategies: Detect Remote Access via USB Hardware (TinyPilot, PiKVM)
description: An adversary may use legitimate remote access hardware to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.

name: XSL Script Processing
detection_strategies: Detect XSL Script Abuse via msxsl and wmic
description: Adversaries may bypass application control and obscure execution of code by embedding scripts inside XSL files. Extensible Stylesheet Language (XSL) files are commonly used to describe the processing and rendering of data within XML files.

name: Template Injection

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Template Injection Detection - Windows
description: Adversaries may create or modify references in user document templates to conceal malicious code or force authentication attempts. For example, Microsoft’s Office Open XML (OOXML) specification defines an XML-based format for Office documents (.docx, xlsx, .pptx) to replace older binary formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt).

name: File and Directory Permissions Modification
detection_strategies: Multi-Platform File and Directory Permissions Modification Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files. File and directory permissions are commonly managed by ACLs configured by the file or directory owner, or users with the appropriate permissions.

name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification
detection_strategies: Windows DACL Manipulation Behavioral Chain Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files. File and directory permissions are commonly managed by ACLs configured by the file or directory owner, or users with the appropriate permissions.

name: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification
detection_strategies: Unix-like File Permission Manipulation Behavioral Chain Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files. File and directory permissions are commonly managed by ACLs configured by the file or directory owner, or users with the appropriate permissions.

name: Execution Guardrails
detection_strategies: Multi-Platform Execution Guardrails Environmental Validation Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may use execution guardrails to constrain execution or actions based on adversary supplied and environment specific conditions that are expected to be present on the target. Guardrails ensure that a payload only executes against an intended target and reduces collateral damage from an adversary’s campaign.

name: Environmental Keying
detection_strategies: Environmental Keying Discovery-to-Decryption Behavioral Chain Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may environmentally key payloads or other features of malware to evade defenses and constraint execution to a specific target environment.

name: Mutual Exclusion
detection_strategies: Detection of Mutex-Based Execution Guardrails Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may constrain execution or actions based on the presence of a mutex associated with malware. A mutex is a locking mechanism used to synchronize access to a resource. Only one thread or process can acquire a mutex at a given time.

name: Domain Trust Discovery
detection_strategies: Detection of Domain Trust Discovery via API, Script, and CLI Enumeration
description: Adversaries may attempt to gather information on domain trust relationships that may be used to identify lateral movement opportunities in Windows multi-domain/forest environments. Domain trusts provide a mechanism for a domain to allow access to resources based on the authentication procedures of another domain.

name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification
detection_strategies: Detection of Domain or Tenant Policy Modifications via AD and Identity Provider
description: Adversaries may modify the configuration settings of a domain or identity tenant to evade defenses and/or escalate privileges in centrally managed environments.

name: Group Policy Modification
detection_strategies: Detection of Group Policy Modifications via AD Object Changes and File Activity
description: Adversaries may modify Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to subvert the intended discretionary access controls for a domain, usually with the intention of escalating privileges on the domain. Group policy allows for centralized management of user and computer settings in Active Directory (AD).

name: Trust Modification
detection_strategies: Detection of Trust Relationship Modifications in Domain or Tenant Policies
description: Adversaries may add new domain trusts, modify the properties of existing domain trusts, or otherwise change the configuration of trust relationships between domains and tenants to evade defenses and/or elevate privileges.Trust details, such as whether or not user identities are federated, allow authentication and autho…

name: Data Destruction
detection_strategies: Detection of Data Destruction Across Platforms via Mass Overwrite and Deletion Patterns
description: Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources. Data destruction is likely to render stored data irrecoverable by forensic techniques through overwriting files or data on local and remote drives.

name: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
detection_strategies: Detection of Lifecycle Policy Modifications for Triggered Deletion in IaaS Cloud Storage
description: Adversaries may modify the lifecycle policies of a cloud storage bucket to destroy all objects stored within. Cloud storage buckets often allow users to set lifecycle policies to automate the migration, archival, or deletion of objects after a set period of time.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
detection_strategies: Detection of Multi-Platform File Encryption for Impact
description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or on large numbers of systems in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources. They can attempt to render stored data inaccessible by encrypting files or data on local and remote drives and withholding access to a decryption key.

name: Service Stop
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection for Service Stop across Platforms
description: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable to legitimate users. Stopping critical services or processes can inhibit or stop response to an incident or aid in the adversary's overall objectives to cause damage to the environment.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection for T1490 - Inhibit System Recovery
description: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

name: Defacement
detection_strategies: Defacement via File and Web Content Modification Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may modify visual content available internally or externally to an enterprise network, thus affecting the integrity of the original content. Reasons for Defacement include delivering messaging, intimidation, or claiming (possibly false) credit for an intrusion.

name: Internal Defacement
detection_strategies: Internal Website and System Content Defacement via UI or Messaging Modifications
description: An adversary may deface systems internal to an organization in an attempt to intimidate or mislead users, thus discrediting the integrity of the systems. This may take the form of modifications to internal websites or server login messages, or directly to user systems with the replacement of the desktop wallpaper.

name: External Defacement
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection of External Website Defacement across Platforms
description: An adversary may deface systems external to an organization in an attempt to deliver messaging, intimidate, or otherwise mislead an organization or users. External Defacement may ultimately cause users to distrust the systems and to question/discredit the system’s integrity.

name: Firmware Corruption
detection_strategies: Firmware Modification via Flash Tool or Corrupted Firmware Upload
description: Adversaries may overwrite or corrupt the flash memory contents of system BIOS or other firmware in devices attached to a system in order to render them inoperable or unable to boot, thus denying the availability to use the devices and/or the system.

name: Resource Hijacking
detection_strategies: Resource Hijacking Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may leverage the resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. Resource hijacking may take a number of different forms.

name: Compute Hijacking
detection_strategies: Multi-Platform Behavioral Detection for Compute Hijacking
description: Adversaries may leverage the compute resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. One common purpose for Compute Hijacking is to validate transactions of cryptocurrency networks and earn virtual currency.

name: Bandwidth Hijacking
detection_strategies: Detect Excessive or Unauthorized Bandwidth Usage for Botnet, Proxyjacking, or Scanning Purposes
description: Adversaries may leverage the network bandwidth resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

name: SMS Pumping
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Resource Hijacking: SMS Pumping via SaaS Application Logs
description: Adversaries may leverage messaging services for SMS pumping, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

name: Cloud Service Hijacking
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Cloud Service Hijacking via SaaS Abuse
description: Adversaries may leverage compromised software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact hosted service availability.

name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1497 Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
description: Adversaries may employ various means to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments. This may include changing behaviors based on the results of checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a virtual machine environment (VME) or sandbox.

name: System Checks
detection_strategies: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion via System Checks across Windows, Linux, macOS
description: Adversaries may employ various system checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments. This may include changing behaviors based on the results of checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a virtual machine environment (VME) or sandbox.

name: User Activity Based Checks
detection_strategies: Detect User Activity Based Sandbox Evasion via Input & Artifact Probing
description: Adversaries may employ various user activity checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments. This may include changing behaviors based on the results of checks for the presence of artifacts indicative of a virtual machine environment (VME) or sandbox.

name: Time Based Checks
detection_strategies: Detect Time-Based Evasion via Sleep, Timer Loops, and Delayed Execution
description: Adversaries may employ various time-based methods to detect virtualization and analysis environments, particularly those that attempt to manipulate time mechanisms to simulate longer elapses of time. This may include enumerating time-based properties, such as uptime or the system clock.

name: Network Denial of Service
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection of T1498 – Network Denial of Service Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users. Network DoS can be performed by exhausting the network bandwidth services rely on. Example resources include specific websites, email services, DNS, and web-based applications.

name: Direct Network Flood
detection_strategies: Direct Network Flood Detection across IaaS, Linux, Windows, and macOS
description: Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by directly sending a high-volume of network traffic to a target. This DoS attack may also reduce the availability and functionality of the targeted system(s) and network.

name: Reflection Amplification
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Reflection Amplification DoS (T1498.002)
description: Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by reflecting a high-volume of network traffic to a target. This type of Network DoS takes advantage of a third-party server intermediary that hosts and will respond to a given spoofed source IP address. This third-party server is commonly termed a reflector.

name: Endpoint Denial of Service
detection_strategies: Endpoint Resource Saturation and Crash Pattern Detection Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may perform Endpoint Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of services to users. Endpoint DoS can be performed by exhausting the system resources those services are hosted on or exploiting the system to cause a persistent crash condition.

name: OS Exhaustion Flood
detection_strategies: Endpoint DoS via OS Exhaustion Flood Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may launch a denial of service (DoS) attack targeting an endpoint's operating system (OS). A system's OS is responsible for managing the finite resources as well as preventing the entire system from being overwhelmed by excessive demands on its capacity.

name: Service Exhaustion Flood
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Endpoint DoS via Service Exhaustion Flood
description: Adversaries may target the different network services provided by systems to conduct a denial of service (DoS). Adversaries often target the availability of DNS and web services, however others have been targeted as well.

name: Application Exhaustion Flood
detection_strategies: Application Exhaustion Flood Detection Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may target resource intensive features of applications to cause a denial of service (DoS), denying availability to those applications. For example, specific features in web applications may be highly resource intensive.

name: Application or System Exploitation
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Endpoint DoS via Application or System Exploitation
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities that can cause an application or system to crash and deny availability to users. Some systems may automatically restart critical applications and services when crashes occur, but they can likely be re-exploited to cause a persistent denial of service (DoS) condition.

name: Server Software Component

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1505 - Server Software Component
description: Adversaries may abuse legitimate extensible development features of servers to establish persistent access to systems. Enterprise server applications may include features that allow developers to write and install software or scripts to extend the functionality of the main application.

name: SQL Stored Procedures
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for SQL Stored Procedures Abuse via T1505.001
description: Adversaries may abuse SQL stored procedures to establish persistent access to systems. SQL Stored Procedures are code that can be saved and reused so that database users do not waste time rewriting frequently used SQL queries.

name: Transport Agent
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1505.002 - Transport Agent Abuse (Windows/Linux)
description: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft transport agents to establish persistent access to systems.

name: Web Shell

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Web Shell Detection via Server Behavior and File Execution Chains
description: Adversaries may backdoor web servers with web shells to establish persistent access to systems. A Web shell is a Web script that is placed on an openly accessible Web server to allow an adversary to access the Web server as a gateway into a network.

name: IIS Components
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1505.004 - Malicious IIS Components
description: Adversaries may install malicious components that run on Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers to establish persistence. IIS provides several mechanisms to extend the functionality of the web servers.

name: Terminal Services DLL
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1505.005 – Terminal Services DLL Modification (Windows)
description: Adversaries may abuse components of Terminal Services to enable persistent access to systems. Microsoft Terminal Services, renamed to Remote Desktop Services in some Windows Server OSs as of 2022, enable remote terminal connections to hosts.

name: vSphere Installation Bundles
detection_strategies: Detect Abuse of vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) for Persistent Access
description: Adversaries may abuse vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) to establish persistent access to ESXi hypervisors. VIBs are collections of files used for software distribution and virtual system management in VMware environments.

name: Software Discovery
detection_strategies: Multi-Platform Software Discovery Behavior Chain
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of software and software versions that are installed on a system or in a cloud environment.

name: Security Software Discovery
detection_strategies: Security Software Discovery Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of security software, configurations, defensive tools, and sensors that are installed on a system or in a cloud environment. This may include things such as cloud monitoring agents and anti-virus.

name: Backup Software Discovery
detection_strategies: Backup Software Discovery via CLI, Registry, and Process Inspection (T1518.002)
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of backup software or configurations that are installed on a system. Adversaries may use this information to shape follow-on behaviors, such as Data Destruction, Inhibit System Recovery, or Data Encrypted for Impact.

name: Implant Internal Image
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1525 – Implant Internal Image
description: Adversaries may implant cloud or container images with malicious code to establish persistence after gaining access to an environment.

name: Cloud Service Discovery
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Cloud Service Discovery
description: An adversary may attempt to enumerate the cloud services running on a system after gaining access. These methods can differ from platform-as-a-service (PaaS), to infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), or software-as-a-service (SaaS).

name: Steal Application Access Token
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1528 - Steal Application Access Token
description: Adversaries can steal application access tokens as a means of acquiring credentials to access remote systems and resources.

name: System Shutdown/Reboot
detection_strategies: Multi-Platform Shutdown or Reboot Detection via Execution and Host Status Events
description: Adversaries may shutdown/reboot systems to interrupt access to, or aid in the destruction of, those systems. Operating systems may contain commands to initiate a shutdown/reboot of a machine or network device.

name: Data from Cloud Storage
detection_strategies: Multi-Platform Cloud Storage Exfiltration Behavior Chain
description: Adversaries may access data from cloud storage. Many IaaS providers offer solutions for online data object storage such as Amazon S3, Azure Storage, and Google Cloud Storage.

name: Account Access Removal
detection_strategies: Account Access Removal via Multi-Platform Audit Correlation
description: Adversaries may interrupt availability of system and network resources by inhibiting access to accounts utilized by legitimate users. Accounts may be deleted, locked, or manipulated (ex: changed credentials, revoked permissions for SaaS platforms such as Sharepoint) to remove access to accounts.

name: Internal Spearphishing
detection_strategies: Internal Spearphishing via Trusted Accounts
description: After they already have access to accounts or systems within the environment, adversaries may use internal spearphishing to gain access to additional information or compromise other users within the same organization.

name: Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions
detection_strategies: Detection of Adversary Use of Unused or Unsupported Cloud Regions (IaaS)
description: Adversaries may create cloud instances in unused geographic service regions in order to evade detection. Access is usually obtained through compromising accounts used to manage cloud infrastructure.

name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
detection_strategies: Cross-Platform Detection of Data Transfer to Cloud Account
description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data by transferring the data, including through sharing/syncing and creating backups of cloud environments, to another cloud account they control on the same service.

name: Cloud Service Dashboard
detection_strategies: Detection of Cloud Service Dashboard Usage via GUI-Based Cloud Access
description: An adversary may use a cloud service dashboard GUI with stolen credentials to gain useful information from an operational cloud environment, such as specific services, resources, and features.

name: Steal Web Session Cookie
detection_strategies: Detection of Web Session Cookie Theft via File, Memory, and Network Artifacts
description: An adversary may steal web application or service session cookies and use them to gain access to web applications or Internet services as an authenticated user without needing credentials. Web applications and services often use session cookies as an authentication token after a user has authenticated to a website.

name: Pre-OS Boot

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1542 Pre-OS Boot
description: Adversaries may abuse Pre-OS Boot mechanisms as a way to establish persistence on a system. During the booting process of a computer, firmware and various startup services are loaded before the operating system. These programs control flow of execution before the operating system takes control.

name: System Firmware
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1542.001 Pre-OS Boot: System Firmware
description: Adversaries may modify system firmware to persist on systems.The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) and The Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) or Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI) are examples of system firmware that operate as the software interface between the operating system and hardware of a computer.

name: Component Firmware
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1542.002 Pre-OS Boot: Component Firmware
description: Adversaries may modify component firmware to persist on systems. Some adversaries may employ sophisticated means to compromise computer components and install malicious firmware that will execute adversary code outside of the operating system and main system firmware or BIOS.

name: Bootkit
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for File Creation or Modification of Boot Files
description: Adversaries may use bootkits to persist on systems. A bootkit is a malware variant that modifies the boot sectors of a hard drive, allowing malicious code to execute before a computer's operating system has loaded.

name: ROMMONkit
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1542.004 Pre-OS Boot: ROMMONkit
description: Adversaries may abuse the ROM Monitor (ROMMON) by loading an unauthorized firmware with adversary code to provide persistent access and manipulate device behavior that is difficult to detect.

name: TFTP Boot

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1542.005 Pre-OS Boot: TFTP Boot
description: Adversaries may abuse netbooting to load an unauthorized network device operating system from a Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server. TFTP boot (netbooting) is commonly used by network administrators to load configuration-controlled network device images from a centralized management server.

name: Create or Modify System Process
detection_strategies: Detection of System Process Creation or Modification Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may create or modify system-level processes to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. When operating systems boot up, they can start processes that perform background system functions. On Windows and Linux, these system processes are referred to as services.

name: Launch Agent
detection_strategies: Detection of Launch Agent Creation or Modification on macOS
description: Adversaries may create or modify launch agents to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

name: Systemd Service
detection_strategies: Detection of Systemd Service Creation or Modification on Linux
description: Adversaries may create or modify systemd services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. Systemd is a system and service manager commonly used for managing background daemon processes (also known as services) and other system resources.

name: Windows Service
detection_strategies: Detection of Windows Service Creation or Modification
description: Adversaries may create or modify Windows services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. When Windows boots up, it starts programs or applications called services that perform background system functions.

name: Launch Daemon
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Launch Daemon Creation or Modification (macOS)
description: Adversaries may create or modify Launch Daemons to execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. Launch Daemons are plist files used to interact with Launchd, the service management framework used by macOS.

name: Container Service
detection_strategies: Detect persistent or elevated container services via container runtime or cluster manipulation
description: Adversaries may create or modify container or container cluster management tools that run as daemons, agents, or services on individual hosts. These include software for creating and managing individual containers, such as Docker and Podman, as well as container cluster node-level agents such as kubelet.

name: Event Triggered Execution
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection of Event Triggered Execution Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges using system mechanisms that trigger execution based on specific events. Various operating systems have means to monitor and subscribe to events such as logons or other user activity such as running specific applications/binaries.

name: Change Default File Association
detection_strategies: Detect Default File Association Hijack via Registry & Execution Correlation on Windows
description: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by a file type association. When a file is opened, the default program used to open the file (also called the file association or handler) is checked.

name: Screensaver

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detect Screensaver-Based Persistence via Registry and Execution Chains
description: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity. Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
detection_strategies: Detect WMI Event Subscription for Persistence via WmiPrvSE Process and MOF Compilation
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by a Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) event subscription. WMI can be used to install event filters, providers, consumers, and bindings that execute code when a defined event occurs.

name: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
detection_strategies: Detect Shell Configuration Modification for Persistence via Event-Triggered Execution
description: Adversaries may establish persistence through executing malicious commands triggered by a user’s shell. User Unix Shells execute several configuration scripts at different points throughout the session based on events.

name: Trap
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Event Triggered Execution via Trap (T1546.005)
description: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by an interrupt signal. The trap command allows programs and shells to specify commands that will be executed upon receiving interrupt signals.

name: LC_LOAD_DYLIB Addition
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for LC_LOAD_DYLIB Modification in Mach-O Binaries on macOS
description: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by the execution of tainted binaries. Mach-O binaries have a series of headers that are used to perform certain operations when a binary is loaded.

name: Netsh Helper DLL
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Netsh Helper DLL Persistence via Registry and Child Process Monitoring (Windows)
description: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by Netsh Helper DLLs. Netsh.exe (also referred to as Netshell) is a command-line scripting utility used to interact with the network configuration of a system.

name: Accessibility Features

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Accessibility Feature Hijacking via Binary Replacement or Registry Modification
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by accessibility features. Windows contains accessibility features that may be launched with a key combination before a user has logged in (ex: when the user is on the Windows logon screen).

name: AppCert DLLs
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for AppCert DLLs Persistence via Registry Injection
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by AppCert DLLs loaded into processes.

name: AppInit DLLs
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Event Triggered Execution: AppInit DLLs (Windows)
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by AppInit DLLs loaded into processes.

name: Application Shimming
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Application Shimming via sdbinst.exe and Registry Artifacts (Windows)
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.

name: Image File Execution Options Injection
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for IFEO Injection on Windows
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by Image File Execution Options (IFEO) debuggers. IFEOs enable a developer to attach a debugger to an application.

name: PowerShell Profile
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for PowerShell Profile Persistence via profile.ps1 Modification
description: Adversaries may gain persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by PowerShell profiles. A PowerShell profile (profile.ps1) is a script that runs when PowerShell starts and can be used as a logon script to customize user environments.

name: Emond

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Event Triggered Execution via emond on macOS
description: Adversaries may gain persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by the Event Monitor Daemon (emond). Emond is a Launch Daemon that accepts events from various services, runs them through a simple rules engine, and takes action.

name: Component Object Model Hijacking
detection_strategies: Windows COM Hijacking Detection via Registry and DLL Load Correlation
description: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by hijacked references to Component Object Model (COM) objects. COM is a system within Windows to enable interaction between software components through the operating system. References to various COM objects are stored in the Registry.

name: Installer Packages
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1546.016 - Event Triggered Execution via Installer Packages
description: Adversaries may establish persistence and elevate privileges by using an installer to trigger the execution of malicious content. Installer packages are OS specific and contain the resources an operating system needs to install applications on a system.

name: Udev Rules
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1546.017 - Udev Rules (Linux)
description: Adversaries may maintain persistence through executing malicious content triggered using udev rules.

name: Python Startup Hooks
detection_strategies: Linux Python Startup Hook Persistence via .pth and Customize Files (T1546.018)
description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by leveraging Python’s startup mechanisms, including path configuration (`.pth`) files and the `sitecustomize.py` or `usercustomize.py` modules.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
detection_strategies: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution Detection Strategy
description: Adversaries may configure system settings to automatically execute a program during system boot or logon to maintain persistence or gain higher-level privileges on compromised systems. Operating systems may have mechanisms for automatically running a program on system boot or account logon.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_strategies: Detect Registry and Startup Folder Persistence (Windows)
description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to a startup folder or referencing it with a Registry run key. Adding an entry to the "run keys" in the Registry or startup folder will cause the program referenced to be executed when a user logs in.

name: Authentication Package
detection_strategies: Detect LSA Authentication Package Persistence via Registry and LSASS DLL Load
description: Adversaries may abuse authentication packages to execute DLLs when the system boots. Windows authentication package DLLs are loaded by the Local Security Authority (LSA) process at system start. They provide support for multiple logon processes and multiple security protocols to the operating system.

name: Time Providers
detection_strategies: Detect Abuse of Windows Time Providers for Persistence
description: Adversaries may abuse time providers to execute DLLs when the system boots. The Windows Time service (W32Time) enables time synchronization across and within domains. W32Time time providers are responsible for retrieving time stamps from hardware/network resources and outputting these values to other network clients.

name: Winlogon Helper DLL
detection_strategies: Detect Winlogon Helper DLL Abuse via Registry and Process Artifacts on Windows
description: Adversaries may abuse features of Winlogon to execute DLLs and/or executables when a user logs in. Winlogon.exe is a Windows component responsible for actions at logon/logoff as well as the secure attention sequence (SAS) triggered by Ctrl-Alt-Delete.

name: Security Support Provider
detection_strategies: Registry and LSASS Monitoring for Security Support Provider Abuse
description: Adversaries may abuse security support providers (SSPs) to execute DLLs when the system boots. Windows SSP DLLs are loaded into the Local Security Authority (LSA) process at system start.

name: Kernel Modules and Extensions
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Kernel Modules and Extensions Autostart Execution
description: Adversaries may modify the kernel to automatically execute programs on system boot. Loadable Kernel Modules (LKMs) are pieces of code that can be loaded and unloaded into the kernel upon demand. They extend the functionality of the kernel without the need to reboot the system.

name: Re-opened Applications

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detect persistence via reopened application plist modification (macOS)
description: Adversaries may modify plist files to automatically run an application when a user logs in. When a user logs out or restarts via the macOS Graphical User Interface (GUI), a prompt is provided to the user with a checkbox to "Reopen windows when logging back in".

name: LSASS Driver
detection_strategies: Detect unauthorized LSASS driver persistence via LSA plugin abuse (Windows)
description: Adversaries may modify or add LSASS drivers to obtain persistence on compromised systems. The Windows security subsystem is a set of components that manage and enforce the security policy for a computer or domain.

name: Shortcut Modification
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1547.009 – Shortcut Modification (Windows)
description: Adversaries may create or modify shortcuts that can execute a program during system boot or user login. Shortcuts or symbolic links are used to reference other files or programs that will be opened or executed when the shortcut is clicked or executed by a system startup process.

name: Port Monitors
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1547.010 – Port Monitor DLL Persistence via spoolsv.exe (Windows)
description: Adversaries may use port monitors to run an adversary supplied DLL during system boot for persistence or privilege escalation. A port monitor can be set through the AddMonitor API call to set a DLL to be loaded at startup.

name: Print Processors
detection_strategies: Windows Detection Strategy for T1547.012 - Print Processor DLL Persistence
description: Adversaries may abuse print processors to run malicious DLLs during system boot for persistence and/or privilege escalation. Print processors are DLLs that are loaded by the print spooler service, `spoolsv.exe`, during boot.

name: XDG Autostart Entries
detection_strategies: Linux Detection Strategy for T1547.013 - XDG Autostart Entries
description: Adversaries may add or modify XDG Autostart Entries to execute malicious programs or commands when a user’s desktop environment is loaded at login. XDG Autostart entries are available for any XDG-compliant Linux system.

name: Active Setup
detection_strategies: Detect Active Setup Persistence via StubPath Execution
description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a Registry key to the Active Setup of the local machine. Active Setup is a Windows mechanism that is used to execute programs when a user logs in. The value stored in the Registry key will be executed after a user logs into the computer.

name: Login Items
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1547.015 – Login Items on macOS
description: Adversaries may add login items to execute upon user login to gain persistence or escalate privileges. Login items are applications, documents, folders, or server connections that are automatically launched when a user logs in. Login items can be added via a shared file list or Service Management Framework.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism (T1548)
description: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevate privileges to gain higher-level permissions. Most modern systems contain native elevation control mechanisms that are intended to limit privileges that a user can perform on a machine.

name: Setuid and Setgid
detection_strategies: Setuid/Setgid Privilege Abuse Detection (Linux/macOS)
description: An adversary may abuse configurations where an application has the setuid or setgid bits set in order to get code running in a different (and possibly more privileged) user’s context.

name: Bypass User Account Control
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1548.002 – Bypass User Account Control (UAC)
description: Adversaries may bypass UAC mechanisms to elevate process privileges on system. Windows User Account Control (UAC) allows a program to elevate its privileges (tracked as integrity levels ranging from low to high) to perform a task under administrator-level permissions, possibly by prompting the user for confirmation.

name: Sudo and Sudo Caching
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection Strategy for Abuse of Sudo and Sudo Caching
description: Adversaries may perform sudo caching and/or use the sudoers file to elevate privileges. Adversaries may do this to execute commands as other users or spawn processes with higher privileges.

name: Elevated Execution with Prompt
detection_strategies: macOS AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges Elevation Prompt Detection
description: Adversaries may leverage the AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API to escalate privileges by prompting the user for credentials. The purpose of this API is to give application developers an easy way to perform operations with root privileges, such as for application installation or updating.

name: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for Temporary Elevated Cloud Access Abuse (T1548.005)
description: Adversaries may abuse permission configurations that allow them to gain temporarily elevated access to cloud resources.

name: TCC Manipulation
detection_strategies: TCC Database Manipulation via Launchctl and Unprotected SIP
description: Adversaries can manipulate or abuse the Transparency, Consent, & Control (TCC) service or database to grant malicious executables elevated permissions.

name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection Strategy for Use Alternate Authentication Material (T1550)
description: Adversaries may use alternate authentication material, such as password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and application access tokens, in order to move laterally within an environment and bypass normal system access controls.

name: Application Access Token
detection_strategies: Behavioral Detection Strategy for Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token (T1550.001)
description: Adversaries may use stolen application access tokens to bypass the typical authentication process and access restricted accounts, information, or services on remote systems. These tokens are typically stolen from users or services and used in lieu of login credentials.

name: Pass the Hash
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1550.002 - Pass the Hash (Windows)
description: Adversaries may “pass the hash” using stolen password hashes to move laterally within an environment, bypassing normal system access controls. Pass the hash (PtH) is a method of authenticating as a user without having access to the user's cleartext password.

name: Pass the Ticket
detection_strategies: Detection Strategy for T1550.003 - Pass the Ticket (Windows)
description: Adversaries may “pass the ticket” using stolen Kerberos tickets to move laterally within an environment, bypassing normal system access controls. Pass the ticket (PtT) is a method of authenticating to a system using Kerberos tickets without having access to an account's password.

name: Web Session Cookie
detection_strategies: Detect Use of Stolen Web Session Cookies Across Platforms
description: Adversaries can use stolen session cookies to authenticate to web applications and services. This technique bypasses some multi-factor authentication protocols since the session is already authenticated.

name: Unsecured Credentials

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Detect Access or Search for Unsecured Credentials Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may search compromised systems to find and obtain insecurely stored credentials. These credentials can be stored and/or misplaced in many locations on a system, including plaintext files (e.g. Shell History), operating system or application-specific repositories (e.g.

name: Credentials In Files
detection_strategies: Detect Access to Unsecured Credential Files Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may search local file systems and remote file shares for files containing insecurely stored credentials.

name: Credentials in Registry
detection_strategies: Detect Credential Discovery via Windows Registry Enumeration
description: Adversaries may search the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs.

name: Shell History
detection_strategies: Detect Access and Parsing of .bash_history Files for Credential Harvesting
description: Adversaries may search the command history on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. On Linux and macOS systems, shells such as Bash and Zsh keep track of the commands users type on the command-line with the "history" utility. Once a user logs out, the history is flushed to the user's history file.

name: Private Keys
detection_strategies: Detect Suspicious Access to Private Key Files and Export Attempts Across Platforms
description: Adversaries may search for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. Private cryptographic keys and certificates are used for authentication, encryption/decryption, and digital signatures.

name: Cloud Instance Metadata API

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
Disable or Remove Feature or Program

detection_strategies: Detect Access to Cloud Instance Metadata API (IaaS)
description: Adversaries may attempt to access the Cloud Instance Metadata API to collect credentials and other sensitive data.

name: Group Policy Preferences
detection_strategies: Detect Access and Decryption of Group Policy Preference (GPP) Credentials in SYSVOL
description: Adversaries may attempt to find unsecured credentials in Group Policy Preferences (GPP). GPP are tools that allow administrators to create domain policies with embedded credentials. These policies allow administrators to set local accounts. These group policies are stored in SYSVOL on a domain controller.

name: Container API

mitigations.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

detection_strategies: Detect Abuse of Container APIs for Credential Access
description: Adversaries may gather credentials via APIs within a containers environment. APIs in these environments, such as the Docker API and Kubernetes APIs, allow a user to remotely manage their container resources and cluster components.

name: Chat Messages
detection_strategies: Detect Unsecured Credentials Shared in Chat Messages
description: Adversaries may directly collect unsecured credentials stored or passed through user communication services.

name: Subvert Trust Controls
detection_strategies: Detect Subversion of Trust Controls via Certificate, Registry, and Attribute Manipulation
description: Adversaries may undermine security controls that will either warn users of untrusted activity or prevent execution of untrusted programs. Operating systems and security products may contain mechanisms to identify programs or websites as possessing some level of trust.

name: Gatekeeper Bypass
detection_strategies: Detect Gatekeeper Bypass via Quarantine Flag and Trust Control Manipulation
description: Adversaries may modify file attributes and subvert Gatekeeper functionality to evade user prompts and execute untrusted programs. Gatekeeper is a set of technologies that act as layer of Apple’s security model to ensure only trusted applications are executed on a host.

name: Code Signing
detection_strategies: Detect Suspicious or Malicious Code Signing Abuse
